title: The Implicit Bias of Adam and Muon on Smooth Homogeneous Neural Networks
claim: The margin that grows during training depends on the optimizer, with each optimizer maximizing its own norm, and iterates converge in direction.
layout: 4 line plots in one row, log-scale axes, panel (a) triplet plus (b)
description: A single row of four line plots. Panel (a) is three plots sharing a log-scaled x-axis of loss, running from 10^3 down to 10^-7. Their y-axes are the l2 margin, the l-infinity margin and a hybrid spectral-norm margin, all on log scales. Each plot has curves for Adam (green), Muon (red), NGD (blue) and Signum (orange). Light and dark shades mark the two activations, dashed lines mark runs without momentum, and shaded bands show variation across seeds. Curves rise sharply and then plateau. The relative ordering of the optimizers changes from one margin to the next. Panel (b) plots cosine similarity to the last iterate (0.8 to 1.0) against normalized step (0 to 1). All curves rise to 1, with NGD rising fastest. A legend sits in the first plot.
caption: (a) Margin values vs. loss for different optimizers. A lighter/darker color signifies the squared-ReLU / ReLU activations respectively. Dotted lines represent optimizers with momentum disabled. Lines are mean values over 10 random seeds, while filled areas represent one standard deviation. (b) Cosine similarity to last iterate $\angles{\frac{\thetab_t}{\norm{\thetab_t}_2}}{\frac{\thetab_{last}}{\norm{\thetab_{last}}_2}}$, plotted on a normalized linear time scale.
abstract: We study the implicit bias of momentum-based optimizers on smooth homogeneous models. We show that \textit{momentum steepest descent} algorithms like Muon (spectral norm), MomentumGD ($\ell_2$ norm), and Signum ($\ell_\infty$ norm) are \textit{approximate} steepest descent trajectories under a decaying learning rate schedule, proving that these algorithms have a bias towards KKT points of the corresponding margin maximization problem. We extend the analysis to Adam (without the stability constant), which maximizes the $\ell_\infty$ margin, and to Muon-Signum and Muon-Adam, which maximize a hybrid norm. Our experiments corroborate the theory and show that the identity of the margin maximized depends on the choice of optimizer. Overall, our results extend earlier lines of work on steepest descent in homogeneous models and momentum-based optimizers in linear models.
